response.original_title: The Shoop Site: Excavating Pennsylvania's Largest Paleoindian Site
response.overview: Hidden beneath a quiet ridge in central Pennsylvania lies one of the largest and most artifact-rich Paleoindian sites in North America. The Shoop Site documents the archaeological significance of this 40-acre Ice Age landscape, where over 100 fluted projectile points and hundreds of tools have been unearthed—evidence of some of the earliest human activity in the Northeast. Blending field footage, expert interviews, and rare artifact visuals, this short documentary explores the lives of the continent’s first hunters and their enduring legacy. Through the lens of excavation and interpretation, the film uncovers how Shoop is reshaping what we know about the First Americans—and why this fragile site deserves closer study and long-term preservation.
